author: Gmelin, 1788
status: 나그네새, 해마다 수십 마리 · 여름에도 드물게 기록
habitat: 나무 위, 큰 나무 밑동의 굴과 건물 틈(둥지 자리)
summary: 주로 나무 위에서 지내는 찌르레기로, 봄에 도래지에 오면 짝을 짓고 번식기에는 암수가 함께 지내다가 번식이 끝나면 무리를 이룬다. 큰 나무 밑동이 패어 생긴 굴이나 건물 틈에 둥지를 틀며, 여러 쌍이 한 건물에 함께 둥지를 짓기도 한다. 5~6월에 한배에 알을 4~5개 낳고, 먹이는 쇠찌르레기와 비슷하다. 동양구, 중국 남부, 인도차이나 북부에서 번식하고 인도차이나, 타이, 말레이반도, 하이난섬, 타이완 등지에서 겨울을 난다.

art.subject: White-shouldered Starling (Sturnus sinensis), adult male, as seen in Korea on spring passage: head pale greyish-white with a faint buffy-brown tinge on the forehead and face; throat greyish-white; back pale grey; rump and uppertail coverts greyish-white; breast pale grey, belly and undertail coverts white; wings black with a bronze gloss and a large white patch on the wing coverts forming a white shoulder; tail black with narrow pale tips to the feathers. Bill slender and blue-grey, bluish at the base; iris whitish; legs bluish-grey.
art.pose: perched high in a tree, side view
art.scene: Korean spring: the crown of a large tree with a hollow at the base of its trunk; no people, buildings or text
views: adult male, side view perched: pale greyish-white head, grey back, large white shoulder patch on the black, bronze-glossed wings, white belly and undertail coverts, black tail, grey bill with bluish base, bluish legs
adult male, head detail in side view: slightly brownish face, bluish-white iris, slender grey bill with a bluish base
art.build: Small, compact starling, about 18cm, clearly smaller than a White-cheeked Starling, with a rounded head and no crest, a short square tail, pointed wings and a slender, pointed bill a little shorter than the head. Legs medium-length, bluish-grey. Perches high in trees. In flight the white wing-covert patch flashes against the black wings, and the pale rump contrasts with the dark tail.
avoid: Do not paint a dark glossy body; the head and body are pale grey and white.
Do not omit the large white patch on the male's wing coverts, the feature that gives the species its name.
Do not paint white cheeks on a dark head (White-cheeked Starling) or a chestnut cheek patch (Chestnut-cheeked Starling).
Do not paint a yellow bill or orange legs.
